decisions.reason: The polarization proof uses only the squared isometry and representation independence, so the cross identity is sound. F4 and step 3.1 nevertheless attributed a conditional-expectation interface to the supplier that its exported statement does not contain; the repair now describes conditional expectation only as an inherited proof-level AC use.

The supplier's phrase that the Riemann--Stieltjes integral exists imports its declared definition, where existence is precisely a common mesh limit for arbitrary tagged partitions. More decisively, the supplier proof's final step explicitly proves that every sufficiently fine tagged sum is close to the same unique value. F2 is therefore an accurate consequence of the complete supplied interface, and the counterexample's left/right mismatch is valid.

The proof establishes equality at all times on a specified measurable probability-one event by rational-time agreement and continuity. On a noncomplete space this does not imply that the entire equality set is measurable, which the library definition of indistinguishability requires. The statement therefore asserted a stronger, potentially undefined conclusion; it now states exactly the common-full-event uniqueness proved.

The quadratic-variation theorem and localized-integral definition both require completeness and right continuity, while (H) alone permits the raw natural filtration. Thus the displayed localized integral and theorem application were not licensed under the stated hypotheses. Adding the usual conditions restores the exact supplier hypotheses and leaves the computation t^3/3 unchanged.

The generated-sigma-algebra and rectangle constructions are choice-free after their inputs are fixed, but the item cited a filtration interface whose global contract assumes AC for its conditional-expectation clause. The unqualified no-choice sentence therefore misstated inherited assumptions, although none of the actual measurability conclusions failed.

The constant process is not elementary because the elementary convention forces value zero at time zero. It is, however, equal in the product-measure L2 class to the elementary representative 1_(0,T]. The repair uses that representative and also makes the localized-integral theorem's usual-conditions hypothesis explicit.

The library convention indexes a sequence by all natural numbers beginning at zero, but the local-martingale clause displayed only tau_1,tau_2,... and quantified an unbounded n. The definition now explicitly uses (tau_n)_{n>=0}, includes tau_0 in the monotonicity requirement, and quantifies every n>=0.

The weak-convergence interface quantifies only over bounded continuous real functions, so it cannot literally be invoked on the complex exponential. The argument is valid after applying that interface separately to cos(tx) and sin(tx), whose two expectation limits combine to characteristic-function convergence.

Every elementary process vanishes at time zero, so neither the literal constant process nor 1-G^n is elementary as written. Their product-measure classes do have elementary representatives: 1_(0,T] and 1_(0,T]-G^n. Replacing the process-level assertions by these representatives preserves the density proof.

The C-infinity conclusion is true for bounded Borel data at positive heat times, but the carrier only dominated two spatial derivatives and one time derivative. The repair proves the polynomial-times-Gaussian formula and a locally uniform integrable bound for every mixed kernel derivative, licensing arbitrary differentiation.

The statement and representation theorem consistently require a local martingale whose paths are cadlag on one full-measure event, but the title omitted that hypothesis and thereby advertised a broader assertion. Adding 'Cadlag' to the title makes the page interface match the proved scope without changing the sound proof.

The proof's existence, isometry, and conditional-expectation suppliers F1, F2, and F3 are all explicitly stated under AC. Saying choice entered only through F4 both hid those inherited hypotheses and asked the bare choice axiom to provide unrelated interfaces. The repair records AC as an ambient assumption inherited through F1--F3.

Standing hypothesis (H) does not imply completeness or right continuity, whereas the continuous-Ito-process definition, localized-integrability definition, localized integral, and Ito formula require the usual conditions. Moreover almost-sure continuity alone does not make the given representative predictable. The repaired statement imposes the usual conditions and uses the F0-normalized continuous representative.

Hypothesis (H) gives adaptedness but only almost-sure path continuity; a null-path modification can destroy joint predictability while preserving (H). The Ito-process and localized-integral interfaces also require the usual conditions. The repair imposes them, normalizes B on its F0 continuity event, and represents the constant integrand class by 1_(0,T].

The correct identity is valid, but under AC and (H) alone the cited localized-integral definition and theorem are unavailable because they require a usual filtration, and an a.s.-continuous Brownian representative need not be predictable. The repaired counterexample states the usual conditions and uses the F0-normalized continuous representative required by its repaired supplier.

The library's local-martingale definition is explicitly real-valued, so the phrase 'R^d-valued continuous local martingale' did not itself entail that each coordinate satisfied the scalar hypothesis used in step 1.1. The statement now directly assumes an adapted continuous vector process whose coordinates are real continuous local martingales.

Clause 4 advertised every continuous finite-variation process but assumed only an absolutely continuous path representation, excluding continuous singular paths such as the Cantor function. The intended stronger result is valid: total variation directly bounds every sum of absolute A-increments, so the proof now covers all continuous bounded-variation paths.

For d>1 the scalar standing hypothesis (H) does not state that the whole vector increment is independent of F_s, and usual conditions add no independence. Thus the identity-dispersion vector Ito process used by F1 was unlicensed. The statement now assumes adaptedness and vector increment independence explicitly, which implies (H) coordinatewise.

Clause 5's word 'below' could be read as promising a quadratic-covariation definition inside this carrier, but no such clause occurs here. The definition really refers to the separate next item on the owning page. The repaired sentence names that page relationship explicitly and disclaims an internal definition.

The bare Axiom of Choice supplies choice functions, not Brownian motion, a filtration, or Gaussian increment laws. Those objects and the vector filtration condition are hypotheses of this theorem. F7 and step 6.1 now restrict the AC bookkeeping to inherited conditional-expectation interfaces and Countable Choice for the Riemann/Lebesgue comparison.

AC asserts the existence of choice functions; it does not create the shifted Brownian coordinate process, its usual filtration, hypothesis (H), or the data required by Dynkin's formula. F5 and the final proof step now identify Brownian structure as stated input and restrict AC bookkeeping to cited interfaces and inherited Countable Choice.
